absent: Locking, concurrency and sleep context for framebuffer, fcntl and floppy paths are not shown.
VESA blanking base values and fb_bitfield layout are not in these fragments.
Numeric value of the Linux-specific fcntl base and pipe, lease, notify, seal, hint and delegation enforcement semantics are not shown.
Floppy ioctl numbers, direction and size encoding beyond symbolic association are not specified here.
Timing units for drive spinup expressed in jiffies and FDC register meanings beyond field names are not shown.

findings.text: Mode activation uses separate bit values for deferring application until next vertical blank, deferring colormap change until blank, affecting all consoles on the display, forcing application without change detection, invalidating the current video mode, and a virtual-terminal text path, plus one obsolete text-acceleration marker.
Synchronization timing uses independent bits for horizontal polarity, vertical polarity, external source, composite polarity, broadcast timings, and sync-on-green behavior.

Video mode selection distinguishes noninterlaced, interlaced, double scan, and odd-field-first ordering within a low-byte mask, with separate higher bits requesting vertical wrap instead of panning and a shared bit whose meaning depends on context as smooth horizontal panning or suppression of offset updates.
Display rotation is a small ordinal with four positions for unrotated, clockwise, upside-down, and counter-clockwise orientation.
Time conversion between pixel clock in picoseconds and frequency in kilohertz is reciprocal around one billion, so either helper divides that constant by its argument.

Variable screen state carries visible and virtual extents, virtual-to-visible offsets, depth and grayscale or format selector, per-channel field descriptors plus transparency, nonstandard format marker, activation request, physical dimensions in millimetres, obsolete acceleration flags, full timing margins and sync lengths with pixel clock, sync and mode selectors, rotation, colorspace, and trailing reserved words for future growth.

Colormap transfer describes a start index and entry count with separate user pointers for red, green, blue and optional transparency, while console mapping binds one console number to one framebuffer number.

Blanking progresses from unblanked through normal blank to deeper suspend and powerdown states distinguished by whether horizontal and vertical sync remain driven, with each named level derived from a corresponding VESA power level.

Vertical-blank reporting separates current in-blank and in-sync conditions from capability bits announcing detectable vertical or horizontal blanks, availability of global and per-axis counters, validity of line and dot positions, and detectable vertical syncs.
Blank status pairs the flag word above with a retrace counter since boot, current scanline and dot coordinates, and reserved words.

Accelerated drawing uses a copy rectangle with destination, size and source origin, a fill rectangle with destination, size, color and raster operation, and an image blit with destination, size, foreground and background colors for monochrome sources, depth, data pointer and embedded colormap; raster operations distinguish plain copy from exclusive-or.

Hardware cursor control selects which fields are valid through separate bits for image, position, hotspot, colormap, shape and size plus an all-fields selector, then carries enable state, raster operation, mask pointer, hotspot coordinate, and an embedded image.
Backlight interface defines a level count of one hundred twenty eight and a maximum value of two hundred fifty five.

Linux-specific file control commands form a dense family built as successive offsets from a shared base, covering leases, directory notification, duplicate-descriptor queries, creation queries, lock cancellation, close-on-exec duplication, pipe sizing, seals, read-write hints, and delegations.
File seals are independent bits preventing further sealing, shrinking, growing, immediate writes, future writes while mapped, and execution-bit changes respectively.
Write lifetime hints form an ordered six-level scale from unset through none, short, medium, long and extreme, with the file-operation alias sharing the unset level value.
Delegation state is a compact record with a flags word required to be zero, a lock-type selector, and a padding half-word required to be zero.

Directory change notification uses one bit per event class for access, modification, creation, removal, rename and attribute change, plus a high persistent-subscription bit that keeps the notifier installed.

Path-relative operations share a negative directory descriptor meaning current working directory, distinct negative descriptors for current thread, thread-group leader, pidfs root, nsfs root, failfs root and an invalid marker, and bit flags controlling symlink following, automount suppression, empty-path handling, statx synchronization strength, recursive application, rename exchange or noreplace or whiteout, effective-id access checks, directory removal, handle identity and uniqueness or connectability, and execution-permission-only checks.

Floppy geometry packs total size, sectors per track, head and track counts, a stretch field whose low bits encode double stepping, side swapping, zero-based numbering and a shifted first-sector base, plus gap sizes, a rate byte encoding perpendicular mode, double-density marker and size-code-derived sector size, stepping and head timing, format gap, and a name pointer used only for predefined formats.
Floppy parameter ioctls clear, set, define and query the geometry record, with media-parameter aliases sharing the set and define paths, and separate toggles enable or disable driver messages.
Formatting uses a fill-byte constant and a descriptor naming device, head and track, bracketed by begin and end commands around a per-track format command that consumes that descriptor.

Error policy carries separate thresholds for aborting, whole-track reads, reset, recalibration and console reporting, adjustable through dedicated set and query ioctls plus a message-threshold and cache-flush command.

Drive parameters combine CMOS type, data-rate ceiling, head load and unload and step timings, spinup and spindown intervals with stop position, select delay, rotation rate, track limit, interrupt timeout, sector interleave, embedded error thresholds, flag bits for messaging, broken or inverted or silent disk-change handling and debugging, a read-track probe selector, a fixed eight-slot autodetect table, change-check frequency and native format, with set and query ioctls and a sixteen-byte drive-name query.

Drive liveness is tracked by ordered status bits for required maintenance action, write-protection probing, unacknowledged versus acknowledged media change, writability, and a fail-open request, exposed as derived mask constants over instantaneous and polled status queries.

Runtime drive state pairs those status flags with spinup, select and first-read timestamps, probed format, current track, highest block and half-track observed, media-generation counter, keep-data retention count, reference and device identity, last media-check time, and DMA buffer pointer with block count.
Controller reset offers conditional, obsolete raw-command, and unconditional modes through one command.

Controller state records last specification bytes, data transfer rate, version and output register copies, I/O address, bitfields for raw-command progress, reset need, configuration need, perpendicular mode, FIFO presence and driver version, plus per-unit head positions, with a dedicated query ioctl.

Write-error accounting counts only attempted physical failures rather than failed system calls, retains first and last failing sector with generation tags and the peak retry count, and is cleared or read through paired ioctls.

Several fields are explicitly obsolete, informational-only, or reserved for growth, and user code must compare the reported controller driver version against its built-in expectation to tolerate larger future structures rather than assuming fixed sizes.
